references.text: The immediate context: Jesus led them out toward Bethany, blessed them, and was taken up into heaven ([ref:Luk 24:50-51|Luke 24:50-51]). The disciples' worship and joy in verse 52 is the direct response to this ascension.

Acts provides a parallel account of Jesus' ascension and the disciples' return to Jerusalem ([ref:Apg 1:9-12|Acts 1:9-12]). Here too, they return to Jerusalem after the ascension, just as Jesus had commanded them.

After the resurrection, the disciples worshiped Jesus when they met him ([ref:Matt 28:9|Matthew 28:9]). The word προσκυνήσαντες (worshiped) in Luke 24:52 expresses this same worship of the risen and exalted Christ.

When the disciples saw the risen Jesus on the mountain in Galilee, they worshiped him ([ref:Matt 28:17|Matthew 28:17]). This parallels the worship described in Luke 24:52, where the disciples worship Jesus at his ascension.

Jesus had promised the disciples: "Your hearts shall rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you" ([ref:Joh 16:22|John 16:22]). The great joy (μετὰ χαρᾶς μεγάλης) that the disciples had when they returned to Jerusalem is the fulfillment of this promise.
The early church continued with joy and praise in the temple after Pentecost ([ref:Apg 2:46-47|Acts 2:46-47]), which is a continuation of the joy and temple service described in Luke 24:52-53.

The angel announced "great joy" (χαρὰν μεγάλην) at Jesus' birth ([ref:Luk 2:10|Luke 2:10]). The Gospel of Luke is framed by this great joy—it begins with the joy over Jesus' coming and ends with the great joy over his completed work of salvation and ascension.

At Jesus' entry into Jerusalem, the disciples praised God with joy for all the mighty works they had seen ([ref:Luk 19:37|Luke 19:37]). The joy in Luke 24:52 is an even greater joy, because it is connected to the resurrection and ascension.

Peter writes about rejoicing with an inexpressible and glorious joy even without seeing Christ ([ref:1 Pet 1:8|1 Peter 1:8]). The disciples' joy in Luke 24:52 shows that Jesus' physical absence at his ascension did not diminish, but rather strengthened their joy.

Jesus commanded the disciples not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the Father's promise ([ref:Apg 1:4|Acts 1:4]). The fact that the disciples returned to Jerusalem (ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ) in Luke 24:52 shows their obedience to this command.
